name: Census Bureau Building Permits Survey (BPS)
gap: US-wide replacement for the NYC-only development pillar (housing_database, rezonings pull from NYC DOB/DCP and have no equivalent outside NYC).
granularity: State, CBSA, county, and permit-issuing place. No tract/block-group level found. This is coarser than the project's current NTA-level comparison set -- within one NYC borough it would only ever distinguish a handful of county-level values, which backend/CLAUDE.md's 'every metric is a percentile within its comparison set' rule would make close to meaningless at NTA granularity. It only becomes useful once the project's planned area-model migration lands and the comparison set becomes the area's CBSA (per backend/CLAUDE.md) -- at CBSA/county granularity across many metros, it's a legitimate signal.
update_frequency: Monthly (preliminary), revised monthly figures on the 18th workday of each month, plus annual totals.
history: Decades (the survey has run continuously since the 1960s/1970s depending on series).
license: US government work, public domain, no restriction found.
cost: Free. No official JSON API confirmed at api.census.gov for this specific dataset -- data is published as bulk text/CSV files under www2.census.gov/econ/bps/, same bulk-file pattern this project already uses for zillow_research.py, so a plain file fetch would work without needing the Census API or a key at all for this particular source (unlike census_acs.py, which does use the keyed API for ACS).

correlation.reason_not_computed: app/research/evaluate_series.py does not exist yet. Also, as a county/CBSA-level series it can't be correlated against this project's current NTA-level FHFA/ZORI comparison without first building the area-model migration's CBSA-level frame.

recommendation: Provisional -- don't implement yet. The source itself is clean (free, no login, public domain, long history, monthly cadence), but it doesn't fit the project's current geographic grain: NYC NTAs are far finer than county/CBSA, so BPS would add almost no discriminating signal if forced into the existing 'development' pillar today (a handful of NYC counties/boroughs all sharing one BPS value). Revisit this specific candidate once the area-model/CBSA migration mentioned in backend/CLAUDE.md actually lands -- at that point it becomes one of the stronger national options for the development pillar outside NYC, and should be re-evaluated instead of re-researched from scratch.
evaluated_by: research-analyst routine (via .claude/skills/research-sources/SKILL.md — .claude/agents/research-analyst.md does not exist in this repo)
